rules.data: Phase A split only: analysis/cache/<corpus>_A.parquet; *_B.parquet never opened. Unit = one IR event with kind == 'result'. text None counts as ''.
rules.lengths: chars = Python len(text) (Unicode code points); bytes = len(text.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')); utf16 = UTF-16 code units (len(text.encode('utf-16-le', 'surrogatepass')) // 2), the unit JavaScript String.length counts (Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI are Node/TS harnesses).
rules.tool_class: shell if IR tool == 'shell' (ir.normalize_tool), else other. Who&When code_exec and computerterminal are 'other' under this rule (reported per tool for whowhen).
rules.group: swechat: per-session format from swechat_population.parquet; other corpora: one group named after the corpus. '_all' pools the groups of a corpus.
rules.window_10kb: length in [9728, 10256] inclusive (task). Comparison window [9199, 9727] has the same width and sits immediately below; it is context, not a test. Computed in chars, bytes, utf16.
rules.swechat_dataset_cap: exact: text ends with '\n... [truncated]' and len(text) == 10256; loose: text ends with '... [truncated]' at any length. Applied to every corpus.
rules.markers: regex catalogue MARKERS (name, type, pattern), re.search on result text. Built before computing this file's counts from: the task's list, and exploration of Phase A result text of swechat / aiv_cc / aiv_cu / whowhen (contexts of 'truncat', 'too large', 'omitted', 'exceeds'). cc_local text was never read; the same patterns were applied to it blind. A result can carry several markers; type counts are unions.
rules.any_truncation: result carries >= 1 marker whose type is in loss_types (read_window and read_refusal excluded: pagination / refusal, nothing silently cut).
rules.residual_truncat_word: results whose text matches (?i)truncat but no catalogue marker: content that mentions truncation (code, prose) plus any harness marker the catalogue misses.
rules.retention: for results carrying a marker / type: counts of native_error (true/false/null), exit_code non-null, ir.error_marker(text) by name, and the scaffold exit line (EXIT_LINE) present. Baseline = results of the same cell with no loss-type marker. Key ratios with session-clustered CI: error_marker non-null | native_error true; exit line present | shell.

exit_line.whowhen: ^exitcode: \d+|exited with Unix exit code: \d+|The Unix exit code was: \d+ (search)

rules.exit_line_none: OpenCode, Copilot, aiv_cu: no exit line is written into the result text (OpenCode's exit status is structured: extra.exit -> exit_code column); exit_line is reported null for them.
rules.rates: stats.cluster_rate (num/den per session, session-clustered bootstrap, 1000 draws, seed stats.SEED) and, for the share of sessions with >= 1 hit, stats.wilson(k_sessions, n_sessions). The bootstrap CI of a 0 count is [0, 0]; use the session Wilson upper bound for zeros.
rules.spikes: per corpus (and per swechat format): the 10 most frequent exact lengths with length > 1000, in chars and in bytes, ties broken by smaller length. Per spike: n, sessions, distinct texts, distinct 64-char prefixes and suffixes (md5, never written out), mean count per exact length in [L-50, L+50] excluding L, results with any catalogue marker, tool-class counts.
rules.cap_candidate_rule: a spike is flagged cap_candidate when n >= 5 AND sessions >= 2 AND distinct_prefix64 / n >= 0.5 AND n >= 5 x neighbourhood mean count (or the neighbourhood is empty). Reason: a cap truncates unrelated outputs to one length, so it shows prefix diversity across sessions and an excess over adjacent lengths; repeated identical content (distinct texts ~ 1) and fixed-format outputs (shared prefix) fail it. Fixed after seeing an exploratory top-12 table of (n, sessions, distinct texts) per corpus, before prefix diversity or neighbourhood excess were computed.
